introduction: “By the Holy Spirit is meant the outpouring grace of God and the effulgent rays that emanate from His Manifestation.” From that definition ‘Abdu’l-Bahá draws a great deal: the Spirit is what gives a second life to those who already live, what the apostles received, the only certain criterion of knowledge, the one power able to unite humanity and end war, and the source of healing and of eloquence. A hundred of the guide’s three hundred quotations are given here, ten from each tenth of its length. The hundred beside them are mostly the scriptures these readings stand on and answer: Ezekiel’s valley of bones, the Psalms, John’s Gospel, Acts, Paul’s letters, the Qur’an on the Spirit breathed into Adam, with Milton, Hopkins, Tennyson and Tagore. About one in five raises a difficulty and ends in a question: Locke and John’s letter on testing inspiration, Paine on revelation at second hand, Kant, Marx and Aristotle on what human means can do, Justin and Seneca on philosophers the readings call lifeless.
questions: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá finds the senses, reason and tradition all fallible and rests certainty on the Holy Spirit. Locke says reason must be the last judge, and John’s letter says to test the spirits. How would you tell an inspiration from a strong feeling?

The readings say universal peace is impossible by human and material means. Kant designed institutions for it, and UNESCO looked to education. What have such means achieved, and what do you think they lack?

“The greatest philosophers without this Spirit are powerless.” Justin counted Socrates a Christian before Christ, and Seneca wrote of a holy spirit within. Where do you think the Spirit has been at work outside the religions?
Resurrection, life and paradise are read here as states of the soul. Paul said that if Christ be not risen, preaching is vain. What changes when these words are taken inwardly?
Healing by the Holy Spirit is said to depend on no condition, yet Mark says Jesus could do no mighty work where there was unbelief. What part does the receiver play?
Several prayers ask for the breaths of the Spirit “at every moment”. Paul warns, “Quench not the Spirit.” What in an ordinary week quenches it, and what renews it?

outside.why: “The descent of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles” is explained as grace shining from Christ upon the mirrors of their hearts. The event as Acts tells it: a rushing mighty wind, and cloven tongues like as of fire.

“What is meant by the Holy Spirit?” The question is old. Paul met disciples at Ephesus who said: we have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost. Why has this teaching so often needed explaining to believers themselves?

‘Abdu’l-Bahá defines the Holy Spirit as outpouring grace and rays from the Manifestation. The Qur’an answers the same question with a limit: the Spirit is by command of my Lord, and of knowledge ye have been vouchsafed but little. How much can be said?

When the light falls on “the hearts of craftsmen, it unfoldeth new and unique arts”. Exodus says it of the man who made the tabernacle: I have filled him with the spirit of God, in all manner of workmanship.
The appearance of the light “is conditioned by the colour of that mirror”. Paul: there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.
In the wise it brings forth wisdom, in craftsmen art. Socrates concluded that poets write not by wisdom but by a sort of genius and inspiration.
“What is meant by eternal life is receiving the grace of the Holy Spirit.” Jesus defines it in the same present tense: this is life eternal, that they might know thee.
The life of the spirit consists in “being quickened through the breath of the Holy Spirit”. Jesus: it is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays that her “breath may vivify the souls”. John’s risen Christ: he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.
The Holy Spirit “is the mediator between God and His creation”. Paul names the mediator as a person: the man Christ Jesus. How do the readings relate the Spirit to the one through whom it appears?
It conveys the light of holiness “to sanctified souls”. The Qur’an says of Jesus: We supported him with the holy Spirit.
There must be a mediator bringing the created into relation with “the ‘Unthinkable One’”. John: no man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son hath declared him.
The Holy Spirit brings “life and illumination to all mankind”. Milton begins his poem by asking it for both: what in me is dark illumine, what is low raise and support.
Jesus “declares that man must be born of its quickening and baptized with its living fire”. His words to Nicodemus.
“Souls deprived of that Spirit are accounted as dead, though they are possessed of the human spirit.” The letter to Sardis: thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead.

The quickening spirit “emanates spontaneously” like rays from the sun. Jesus compares it to wind: it bloweth where it listeth, and thou canst not tell whence it cometh. Can what is free in that way be sought, or only received?
“By the Word is not meant the body of Christ but the divine perfections that were manifested in Him.” John’s sentence, which the reading interprets.
Christ is a mirror in which the Sun is seen; “we say it is the sun”. The Nicene Creed will not have a mirror: Light of Light, of one substance with the Father. What does each image protect?
The material nature comes from Adam, the spiritual from the Word. Paul, later in the same chapter: the first Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam a quickening spirit.
The question put to ‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes this verse of Paul, on which his account of the two natures in man is a commentary.
The saying about the unforgivable word against the Holy Ghost, as Matthew gives it.
Human spirits “do not return after death to this world”. Hebrews: it is appointed unto men once to die.

The rational soul does not come back; only the Holy Spirit returns in each dispensation. The Gita teaches that the spirit puts on new bodies as a man puts on new clothes. What do the two teachings each make of the worth of a single life?

That world is one of lights, love and perfections, and all “must be attained during this vanishing existence”. Rabbi Jacob: this world is like a vestibule; prepare yourself in the vestibule, that you may enter the banqueting hall.

The first criterion of knowledge is the senses, which European philosophers “regard … as sacrosanct”. Locke is the philosopher meant: the mind is white paper, and all its furniture comes from experience.
The second is reason. Descartes’s rule: never to accept anything for true which I did not clearly know to be such.

‘Abdu’l-Bahá finds senses, reason and tradition all fallible and looks to the bounty of the Holy Spirit. Locke, writing against “enthusiasm”, held that reason must be our last judge and guide in every thing. Who judges whether an inspiration is from the Spirit?
Only the Holy Spirit gives certainty. John’s letter adds a caution from inside the faith: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God. By what are they to be tried?
Man is enlightened so as “to be the source of guidance to others”. Jesus: ye are the light of the world.
“Baptism through the Holy Spirit.” John the Baptist: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire.
In the prison of Ṭihrán Bahá’u’lláh felt something flow over Him “even as a mighty torrent”. Ezekiel’s call: the spirit entered into me when he spake unto me, and set me upon my feet.
The beginning of a revelation, in chains and darkness. Muḥammad’s began in a cave, with a command he could not at first obey.

Bahá’u’lláh describes an experience no one else could witness. Paine’s objection to every such account: it is revelation to the first person only, and hearsay to every other. On what grounds does a hearer believe a prophet’s report?
The Holy Spirit was “generated through the agency of a single letter”. The Psalm: by the word of the Lord were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.
Whoever is born of the Spirit has attained “life” and “resurrection”. Jesus to Martha: I am the resurrection, and the life.

Resurrection and paradise are read as states of the soul in every dispensation. Paul staked everything on an event: if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain. What is gained and lost by the inward reading?
A single word of his “bestoweth the spirit of holiness upon every mouldering bone”, and a thousand claws hunt him. Jesus over Jerusalem: thou that killest the prophets.
“Methinks that I hear the Voice of the Holy Spirit calling from behind Me.” Elijah heard it after wind, earthquake and fire: a still small voice.
Let them “revive and renew themselves from moment to moment”. Lamentations: his compassions fail not; they are new every morning.
Renewal by the breaths of the Holy Spirit. Paul: though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
“A power above and beyond the powers of nature” is needed to change hatred into love. Paul on nature’s own power: the good that I would I do not.
Human resentments will not mend themselves. Kant, from the side of philosophy: out of such crooked material as man is made of, nothing can be hammered quite straight.

‘Abdu’l-Bahá says only a power beyond nature can turn hatred to fellowship. Aristotle thought character was made by practice: we become just by doing just acts. How much can habit and law do without the Spirit?
Christ’s disciples “became enlightened, spiritual beings”. The council noticed it in two fishermen: they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
“The Holy Spirit is like unto the life in the human body, which blends all differences of parts and members.” Paul: as the body is one, and hath many members, so also is Christ.
If any part is injured, “all the other parts … sympathetically respond”. Paul: whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it.
Through the Holy Spirit “perfect fraternity” becomes practicable. The first church after Pentecost: the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.

The spiritual brotherhood is “higher, holier and superior to all others”. Schiller’s ode makes all men brothers under joy, and the French Revolution tried to do it by decree. What has each kind of brotherhood been able to bear?
The oneness of humanity “is impossible except through the divine power”; “other powers are too weak”. Zechariah: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
Only the Holy Spirit can unite mankind. Marx called on the workers of all countries to unite on the strength of a shared interest. What has interest been able to unite, and where has it stopped?
“Without the spirit the world of mankind is lifeless.” Ezekiel saw bones with sinews and flesh upon them, “but there was no breath in them”.

“Universal peace is an impossibility through human and material agencies.” Kant drew up articles for a perpetual peace founded on law between republics. How much of the peace the world has had is owed to such agencies?
It must be through spiritual power. The Psalm: except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.

Humanity must be “confirmed by the breath of the Holy Spirit in order to receive universal education”. UNESCO’s founders in 1945: the defences of peace must be constructed in the minds of men. Is education enough without what the reading asks for?
Material progress comes by observation, spiritual progress by the Holy Spirit. Tennyson on having one without the other: knowledge comes, but wisdom lingers.
Two kinds of progress. Jesus weighs them: what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

Whoever receives this power “is able to influence all with whom he comes into contact”. Paul: my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power.

“The greatest philosophers without this Spirit are powerless, their souls lifeless.” Justin Martyr thought Socrates and Heraclitus had lived by the Word before Christ came. Is the Spirit absent wherever its name is unknown?
Philosophers without the Spirit are dead of heart. Seneca, a philosopher: God is near you, he is with you, he is within you; a holy spirit indwells within us. What would the reading say he had?
Only “the breaths of the Holy Spirit will heal this world sickness of war”. Joel’s promise: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.

“To gain control over physical bodies is an extremely easy matter, but to bring spirits within the bonds of serenity is a most arduous undertaking.” Proverbs: he that ruleth his spirit is better than he that taketh a city.
Bodies are easily ruled; spirits need a holy power. Machiavelli thought fear sufficient for a prince’s purposes. What can fear not obtain?
“All the powers combined have not the power to establish universal peace.” Micah gives the peace to God’s judging among the nations: they shall beat their swords into plowshares.
The powers cannot withstand “these endless wars”. A general who became president, on what the wars cost: every gun that is made is a theft from those who hunger.
“Divine confirmations are with you and the power of the Holy Spirit sustains you.” The risen Christ: ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you.
God will “aid you to perform an exploit whose like the eye of creation hath never looked upon”. Jeremiah protested that he was a child and was answered: I am with thee.
May each “with an eloquent tongue … set himself to acclaiming”. Jesus: take no thought how or what ye shall speak; it is the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.
An eloquent tongue is hoped for. Moses pleaded that he had none: I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
Children are trees to be watered by the bounty of God under “the Sun of His Holy Spirit”. Isaiah: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and they shall spring up as willows by the water courses.
A Sunday school where the Word of God is recited for children “is indeed a blessed thing”. Moses: thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children.
May your tongues “set forth and expound the inner meanings of the Holy Books”. The two at Emmaus: did not our heart burn within us, while he opened to us the scriptures?
The friends will “make the blind to see, the deaf to hear”. Isaiah’s signs of the promised day, which the reading takes inwardly.
“The Holy Spirit speaketh through the innermost essence of the human tongue.” David’s last words: the Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.
The Spirit speaks through the human tongue. Tagore: this little flute of a reed thou hast breathed through it melodies eternally new.
“We must become attracted to God. The breaths of the Holy Spirit must take effect.” Jesus: no man can come to me, except the Father draw him.
Without that attraction “it is impossible for the teachings of God to accomplish in us”. Portia on knowing the good without the power to do it.
A spirit confirmed by the Holy Spirit “will show its effect in every condition”. Samuel to Saul: the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt be turned into another man.

Through the Holy Spirit this Cause “can break the laws of this contingent world”. Hume’s maxim: no testimony is sufficient to establish a miracle unless its falsehood would be more miraculous. What would he require, and can the claim be put in his terms at all?
In the story Christ flees from a fool whom even the Holy Spirit would not cure. Proverbs: though thou bray a fool in a mortar, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
Even Christ could not help the fool. Mark records a town where he could do no mighty work, and marvelled at their unbelief. What does the Spirit’s power wait upon?
“Christ healed by the power of his word.” At Nazareth he expected the taunt: Physician, heal thyself. Why do healers of this kind so often meet disbelief at home?
“The one who is sick may be in the East, and the healer in the West.” The centurion to Jesus: speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
Healing by the Holy Spirit “is not dependent upon any condition”. James: the prayer of faith shall save the sick.
“Do not take into consideration your own aptitudes and capacities.” Paul: God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the mighty.
God will “endue your souls with the sustaining power of His holy Spirit”. Paul heard: my strength is made perfect in weakness.
If thou be steadfast, “thou wilt find thyself assisted by the angels of heaven”. Joshua: be strong and of a good courage; for the Lord thy God is with thee.
“Although many will arise against you, they shall not prevail!” The promise is Jeremiah’s, word for word.
“As to the ‘white dove,’ it is the Holy Spirit.” Matthew: he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove.
The dove shall flutter over thee. Hopkins: the Holy Ghost over the bent world broods with warm breast and with ah! bright wings.
Divine physicians are to travel and heal “through the power of the Holy Spirit”. Jesus’ charge to the twelve: heal the sick; freely ye have received, freely give.
“That food is the divine advices and exhortations.” Jesus in the wilderness: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
May you “find at every moment a new spirit”. The Psalm: renew a right spirit within me; take not thy holy spirit from me.
“As the sun is to the body of a man so is the Sun of Truth to his soul.” Plato drew the same proportion between the sun and the good.
May you “see the Sun of Truth shining through all material clouds”. Paul: now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.
“Ye have taken on another life.” Paul: if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away.
Ye have gained access to the Threshold of God. Tennyson: Spirit with Spirit can meet; closer is He than breathing, and nearer than hands and feet.
“They are as the body, and Thou art the Spirit of life.” The Qur’an on the making of Adam: when I have breathed into him of My Spirit.
Cause her “to turn away from this mortal world of dust”. Paul: set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
“Give me a new life at every instant.” Ezekiel’s promise: a new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.
The prayer asks for the breaths of the Spirit at every moment. Paul’s brief counsel implies they can be refused: quench not the Spirit. What quenches it?

john-wind-bloweth-where-it-listeth.text: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit

john-breathed-on-them.text: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you. And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost

acts-not-so-much-as-heard.text: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples, He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost

romans-spirit-beareth-witness.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God

corinthians-spirit-is-liberty.text: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty

corinthians-in-adam-all-die.text: For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive

corinthians-quickening-spirit.text: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit

luke-spirit-of-the-lord-is-upon-me.text: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord

isaiah-spirit-of-wisdom.text: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord

numbers-all-the-lords-people-prophets.text: And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord'S people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them

samuel-turned-into-another-man.text: And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man

thessalonians-quench-not-the-spirit.text: Quench not the Spirit. Despise not prophesyings. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good

james-prayer-of-faith.text: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him

matthew-speak-the-word-only.text: The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed

mark-no-mighty-work.text: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. And he marvelled because of their unbelief

exodus-bezaleel.text: See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah: And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship

ezekiel-spirit-entered-into-me.text: And he said unto me, Son of man, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak unto thee. And the spirit entered into me when he spake unto me

samuel-spirit-spake-by-me.text: The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue

john-except-the-father-draw-him.text: No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day

jeremiah-i-am-a-child.text: Then said I, Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child. But the Lord said unto me, Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak. Be not afraid of their faces: for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the Lord

jeremiah-shall-not-prevail.text: And they shall fight against thee; but they shall not prevail against thee; for I am with thee, saith the Lord, to deliver thee

proverbs-bray-a-fool.text: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him

corinthians-temple-of-god.text: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you

mark-what-shall-it-profit.text: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul

quran-supported-with-the-holy-spirit.text: And verily We gave unto Moses the Scripture and We caused a train of messengers to follow after him, and We gave unto Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs (of Allah's sovereignty), and We supported him with the Holy spirit. Is it ever so, that, when there cometh unto you a messenger (from Allah) with that which ye yourselves desire not, ye grow arrogant, and some ye disbelieve and some ye slay?

quran-breathed-of-my-spirit.text: So, when I have made him and have breathed into him of My Spirit, do ye fall down, prostrating yourselves unto him.

quran-strengthened-with-a-spirit.text: Thou wilt not find folk who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His messenger, even though they be their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their clan. As for such, He hath written faith upon their hearts and hath strengthened them with a Spirit from Him, and He will bring them into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide. Allah is well pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him. They are Allah's party. Lo! is it not Allah's party who are the successful?

hopkins-holy-ghost-broods.text: Because the Holy Ghost over the bent / World broods with warm breast and with ah! bright wings
hopkins-holy-ghost-broods.author: Gerard Manley Hopkins

tagore-little-flute.text: This little flute of a reed thou hast carried over hills and dales, and hast breathed through it melodies eternally new
tagore-little-flute.author: Rabindranath Tagore
tagore-little-flute.caveat: Tagore’s own English version of his Bengali poem.

milton-chiefly-thou-o-spirit.text: And chiefly thou, O Spirit, that dost prefer / Before all temples th' upright heart and pure, / Instruct me, for thou know'st; thou from the first / 20Wast present, and, with mighty wings outspread, / Dove-like sat'st brooding on the vast Abyss, / And mad'st it pregnant: what in me is dark / Illumine, what is low raise and support
milton-chiefly-thou-o-spirit.author: John Milton

tennyson-closer-than-breathing.text: Speak to Him thou for He hears, and Spirit with Spirit can meet— / Closer is He than breathing, and nearer than hands and feet
tennyson-closer-than-breathing.author: Alfred Tennyson

locke-reason-last-judge.text: Reason must be our last judge and guide in every thing
locke-reason-last-judge.author: John Locke
